headline: Our DNA Holds Secrets of Two Lost Human Cousins
meta_description: Scientists discover two extinct human lineages hiding in modern DNA, revealing humans interbred with mysterious relatives across Africa and Eurasia.
summary_short: Researchers at UC Berkeley found genetic traces from two previously unknown human ancestors in living people's DNA, reshaping our understanding of human evolution.
body:
A team at UC Berkeley has uncovered something remarkable hidden inside us: genetic material from two extinct human species that no one knew existed until now. Using a new technique that reconstructs ancient genealogical connections from modern genomes, researchers identified specific regions of DNA that came from mysterious ancestors and pinpointed when our relatives interbred with them. One ghost ancestor mixed with modern humans in Africa more than 50,000 years ago, contributing roughly 1% of today's human genome—the same proportion we inherited from Neanderthals. The other discovery is even older: a super-archaic lineage dating back about 1.8 million years that interbred with Denisovans, eventually passing small amounts of its genetic material to modern humans through that connection.

What makes this finding extraordinary is that scientists have no fossils from these populations. Instead of relying on ancient remains, researcher Priya Moorjani's team developed a technique called TRACE that searches for archaic genetic regions using complete genomes from present-day people around the world. By examining how DNA segments connect through shared ancestry across many generations, they reconstructed a detailed evolutionary map our ancestors left behind.

The discovery reveals a far messier, more interconnected human story than the simple branching tree we once imagined. Rather than isolated populations, early humans lived alongside numerous related groups in Africa and Eurasia, encountering and mixing with one another repeatedly across a million years. These populations were genetically similar enough to have children together—and those children's descendants still carry the evidence today. Scientists still don't know exactly who these ghost and super-archaic populations were, though their estimated dates overlap with Middle Pleistocene Homo groups in Africa and Homo erectus populations in Eurasia. The findings, published in Science on July 30, 2026, suggest that mixture among human populations has been far more pervasive throughout our history than anyone previously understood.
quick_facts: Two unknown human ancestors' DNA found in modern genomes
Ghost ancestor interbred with humans in Africa 50,000+ years ago
Super-archaic lineage dates back 1.8 million years
UC Berkeley team used new TRACE method on present-day genomes
Ghost ancestry makes up ~1% of modern human DNA
